dedupe_keys.name: global wui areas 2020 baseline and 1985 to 2020 time series hku datahub

description: This dataset maps global wildland-urban interface areas as a 2020 baseline and as a time series every five years from 1985 to 2020, with separate layers for interface and intermix types. It was produced at the University of Hong Kong, deposited by Bin Chen, for the 2024 Nature Sustainability paper on wildfire risk for global WUI areas, combining fine-resolution housing and vegetation mapping. The paper estimates 6.62 million km2 of WUI worldwide, a 12.56 percent rise from 1985 to 2020, and finds that 7.07 percent of WUI areas, housing 4.47 million people, lie within 2,400 m of wildfire burned areas from 2001 to 2020. Coverage is global. Format and access: GeoTIFF files on the HKU DataHub, a figshare repository, without login. Licence: CC-BY-NC-4.0, so commercial reuse is not allowed; free. Caveats: the resolution was not stated on the pages read, and WUI results depend on the housing and land-cover inputs. It supports wildfire exposure analysis for settlements and the infrastructure serving them. Related catalogue records are the 30 m global WUI maps for 2000 to 2020 and the SILVIS maps for the US.
